title: Cartwise Rewards Member Terms — One Rewards Account per Customer
content:
**Clause.** A customer holds one Cartwise Rewards account. A new enrollment is allowed only when the customer has no rewards account that is not closed.

The limit is 1 rewards account per customer at a time, counted across every account on file for that customer.

## What the clause turns on

| Element | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Whose accounts are counted | Every Cartwise Rewards account recorded under the same customer |
| Which accounts stand in the way | Any account that is not closed — one that is enrolled, active or suspended |
| Which accounts do not | Accounts that are closed |
| What decides it | The company's system record of the customer's rewards accounts and their status, as it stands before the new enrollment is made; a customer's own account of their past membership does not replace it |

## The clause as a decision

- The customer has no Cartwise Rewards account on record → a new enrollment is allowed.
- Every Cartwise Rewards account on record for the customer is closed → a new enrollment is allowed.
- The customer has a Cartwise Rewards account on record that is enrolled, active or suspended → a new enrollment is not allowed.

Because the clause says a new enrollment is allowed *only* when no account that is not closed exists, these three rows exhaust the cases.

## Hypothetical cases

1. A customer's only Cartwise Rewards account was closed for inactivity (hypothetical). No account that is not closed remains, so a new enrollment is allowed.
2. A customer's Cartwise Rewards account is suspended during a misuse review (hypothetical). A suspended account is not closed, so a new enrollment is not allowed while it stands.
3. A customer enrolled but has not yet had a qualifying order, so the account is still enrolled and not yet active (hypothetical). That account is not closed, so a second enrollment is not allowed.

## Basis Q&A

**Does an account that has never become active count?** Yes. An enrolled account is an account that is not closed, and it counts toward the limit of 1.

**Is the limit per household, per card or per customer?** Per customer: the accounts counted are those recorded under that customer.
